chunks: You were the army of a woman, and the followers of a quadruped,
When it grumbled you responded, and when it was wounded (hamstrung) you fled away.
Your character is low and your pledge is broken. Your faith is hypocrisy. Your water is brackish.
He who stays with you is laden with sins and he who forsakes you secures Allah’s mercy secures forsakes you.
As though I see your mosque prominent, resembling the surface of a boat, while Allah has sent chastisement from above and from below it and every one who is on it is drowned.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's condemnation of the people of Basra in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha’s sermon on the people of Basra utilizes vivid metaphorical language, likening their political instability to being 'soldiers of a woman' (Aisha) and 'followers of a camel' during the Battle of the Camel, highlighting their deviation from principled leadership. Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the spiritual peril of those who remained entrenched in their errors with the divine mercy granted to those who departed, framing their city as a vessel of punishment. This critique underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *fiqh al-waqi'* (understanding the reality) and the moral consequences of political opportunism versus steadfastness in faith.
